title: Causal-aware Graph Neural Architecture Search under Distribution Shifts

problem.claim: Graph neural architecture search must design architectures that generalize under distribution shifts.

gap.claim: Existing methods rely on correlations that may be spurious and distribution-dependent, while causal graph-architecture relationships and their use for handling distribution shifts remain unexplored.

contributions.claim: CARNAS captures causal graph-architecture relationships during NAS to discover graph architectures under distribution shifts.
The approach combines Disentangled Causal Subgraph Identification, Graph Embedding Intervention, and Invariant Architecture Customization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CARNAS as a novel approach for causal-aware graph neural architecture search.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets reportedly show that CARNAS enhances out-of-distribution generalization.
The reported improvement is attributed to uncovering causal graph-architecture relationships during NAS.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph neural architecture search designs graph neural network architectures using correlations between graphs and architectures.
Correlation-based methods may use spurious, distribution-dependent relationships and therefore generalize poorly under distribution shifts.
The abstract identifies causal relationship discovery with stable cross-distribution predictive ability and its use in handling shifts as unresolved challenges.
CARNAS addresses the challenges through causal subgraph identification, latent-space graph embedding intervention, and invariant architecture customization.
The authors report improved out-of-distribution generalization on synthetic and real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Relationships that are predictive within observed distributions may be spurious and fail under distribution shifts.

interpretation.claim: Methods intended to generalize across environments should distinguish stable causal structure from distribution-specific correlation.

application.claim: For architecture search under changing data distributions, incorporate mechanisms that identify stable substructures and preserve invariant features.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach is effective beyond the reported synthetic and real-world datasets or under other shift types.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not detail how causal relationships are identified or how distribution shifts are constructed.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, computational cost, or reproducibility.
